title: Algebra and simultaneous equations
description: Rearrange engineering equations and solve for several unknowns without losing signs.
practice_prompt: Solve A + B = 10 and 2A - B = 2; substitute both answers back into the equations.
common_mistake: Moving a term across an equals sign without changing its sign.

check.question: If A + B = 10 and 2A - B = 2, what is A?
check.explanation: Add the equations: 3A = 12, so A = 4 and B = 6.

title: Geometry, trigonometry and radians
description: Read the reference angle, identify perpendicular distances and use radians in rotational relationships.
outcomes: Use sine and cosine with a drawn triangle
practice_prompt: Draw a 3-4-5 triangle, label opposite and adjacent sides, then convert 90 degrees to radians.
common_mistake: Using a memorised sine/cosine rule without checking the reference angle.

check.question: A force F makes an angle theta with the vertical. Which is its horizontal component magnitude?
check.explanation: The horizontal component is opposite the angle measured from the vertical: F sin(theta).

title: Units, dimensions and sign conventions
description: Keep SI units, coordinate directions and physical quantities consistent before calculating.
practice_prompt: Convert 250 mm to metres and 2 kN to newtons. State positive x, y and rotation directions.
common_mistake: Mixing millimetres with metres, or treating a negative answer as automatically wrong.

check.question: What are the SI units of a force moment?
check.explanation: Moment is force times perpendicular distance, so its units are N m.

title: Differentiation and integration
description: Connect rates of change and accumulated quantities using derivatives, definite integrals and initial conditions.
practice_prompt: For v(t) = 3t^2 and s(0) = 2, find a(t) and s(t). Check by differentiating.
common_mistake: Forgetting the initial value or using a constant-acceleration formula for variable acceleration.

check.question: If v(t) = 3t^2, what is a(t)?
check.explanation: Acceleration is dv/dt, so a(t) = 6t.

title: Graphs, slopes and signed areas
description: Interpret gradients, signed area and piecewise functions before using motion and load diagrams.
outcomes: Distinguish signed area and total area
practice_prompt: Sketch a velocity graph that crosses zero. Shade the signed displacement and the total distance separately.
common_mistake: Counting a negative velocity area as positive displacement, or confusing a graph value with its gradient.

check.question: What does the signed area under a velocity-time graph represent?
check.explanation: The signed integral of velocity gives displacement. Total distance uses the magnitude of velocity.

title: Force components and resultants
description: Resolve two-dimensional forces into Cartesian components and reconstruct a resultant with the correct direction.
practice_prompt: Hide a lecture solution. Resolve each force, add components, and reconstruct magnitude and direction.
common_mistake: Using the horizontal-angle component formulas when the diagram measures an angle from the vertical.

check.question: A 100 N force acts 30 degrees above the positive x-axis. What is its vertical component?
check.explanation: Fy = 100 sin(30 degrees) = 50 N because the angle is measured from x.

title: Free-body diagrams
description: Isolate one body and replace each physical support or contact by the external forces it can exert.
practice_prompt: Draw the isolated body before writing equations. Explain each reaction direction and omit internal force pairs for the whole body.
common_mistake: Keeping a support symbol on the isolated body instead of replacing it with reaction forces.

check.question: For a 2D pin support, which reaction model is normally appropriate?
options: Two force components, no reaction couple
check.explanation: An ideal 2D pin restrains translation in x and y but allows rotation.

title: Particle equilibrium
description: Use a correct particle free-body diagram to solve force balance in two dimensions.
practice_prompt: Solve a cable-junction problem, then substitute the tensions into both component equations.
common_mistake: Setting every individual force to zero instead of setting the vector sum to zero.

check.question: For a particle in static equilibrium, which condition must hold?
options: The vector sum of forces is zero
check.explanation: Forces can be nonzero while cancelling in the vector sum.

title: 2D moments and couples
description: Calculate the turning effect of a force, choose a moment centre and distinguish forces from couples.
practice_prompt: Calculate a moment using both F times perpendicular distance and xFy - yFx; compare the signs.
common_mistake: Using the distance to the application point instead of the perpendicular distance to the line of action.

check.question: A force line of action passes through the chosen moment centre. What is its moment about that centre?
options: F times the distance to the application point
It depends on force magnitude only
check.explanation: The perpendicular moment arm is zero.

title: Support reactions and rigid-body equilibrium
description: Combine force and moment equilibrium to find support reactions on a planar rigid body.
outcomes: Model pin, roller and fixed supports
practice_prompt: Find reactions for a loaded beam. Choose a moment centre that removes as many unknowns as possible.
common_mistake: Solving reaction equations before checking the number and direction of unknown support reactions.

check.question: Why take moments about a pin support when solving a beam?
options: Its reaction forces then have zero moment arm
It makes the applied loads vanish
check.explanation: Forces acting at the selected pin have zero moment about that point.

title: Trusses: joints, sections and zero-force members
description: Use two-force-member assumptions, joint equilibrium and strategic section cuts to find axial member forces.
practice_prompt: Find reactions first. Solve one joint with at most two unknowns, then compare with a section through the target member.
common_mistake: Applying the two-force-member model when loads act between the joints.

check.question: At an unloaded joint with only two non-collinear members, what are the member forces?
check.explanation: With no external joint load or support reaction, two non-collinear forces cannot balance unless both are zero.

title: 3D vectors and force along a line
description: Build position and unit vectors from coordinates; distinguish scalar and vector products.
practice_prompt: Write r_AB from point coordinates, normalise it, and multiply by the force magnitude. Check the unit-vector magnitude.
common_mistake: Using coordinates directly as a force direction without first normalising the direction vector.

check.question: For a force of magnitude F from A towards B, which expression is correct?
check.explanation: The unit vector supplies direction; multiplying it by F supplies the magnitude.

title: 3D moments and moment about an axis
description: Use r cross F for a moment vector and project it onto a specified unit axis vector.
outcomes: Project a moment onto an axis
practice_prompt: Calculate the moment vector, then dot it with the unit vector of the requested axis.
common_mistake: Reversing the cross-product order or projecting onto an axis vector that is not a unit vector.

check.question: Which expression gives the scalar moment about an axis with unit vector u?
check.explanation: First obtain the moment vector r cross F, then take its scalar projection onto the unit axis.

title: Distributed loads and equivalent resultants
description: Replace a load distribution with an equivalent resultant at the centroid of its load diagram.
outcomes: Find area under a load diagram
practice_prompt: For a triangular load, find its resultant and distance from the larger-intensity end; then solve a beam reaction problem.
common_mistake: Placing a triangular-load resultant at the midpoint or confusing N/m with N.

check.question: A triangular load grows from zero to w over length L. Its resultant acts where?
check.explanation: The centroid of the triangular load diagram is 2L/3 from the zero-intensity end.

title: 3D particle and rigid-body equilibrium
description: Combine vector force and moment balance with appropriate three-dimensional support models.
practice_prompt: Write all cable forces with unit vectors. Form the force and moment equations before solving unknown magnitudes.
common_mistake: Assuming a 3D support has the same restraint components as a 2D support.

check.question: For a general rigid body in 3D static equilibrium, what must be zero?
options: Only the sum of force magnitudes
Both the resultant force vector and resultant moment vector
check.explanation: A general rigid body needs both vector force and moment balance.

title: Internal forces and section cuts
description: Cut a member and use equilibrium of one side to determine normal force, shear force and bending moment.
practice_prompt: Make a cut before and after a point load. Choose the simpler side and write all three equilibrium equations.
common_mistake: Including a force on the removed side of a cut, or forgetting one internal resultant.

check.question: After cutting a planar beam, what internal resultants generally appear on the cut face?
options: Normal force, shear force and bending moment
check.explanation: The cut transmits axial force N, transverse shear V and bending moment M.

title: Shear-force and bending-moment diagrams
description: Connect distributed loading, section shear and bending moment through slopes, areas and jumps.
practice_prompt: Sketch V and M for a beam with a point load and a distributed load. Check end conditions and the area under V.
common_mistake: Putting the effect of a concentrated couple into the shear diagram instead of the moment diagram.

check.question: Across a concentrated transverse force, what happens to the shear-force diagram?
check.explanation: A point force produces a jump in shear. A concentrated couple produces a jump in bending moment.

title: Centroids and composite areas
description: Locate an area centroid with a common datum, symmetry and signed component areas for cut-outs.
practice_prompt: Build an A, x, y table for a composite shape with a hole. Check that the answer agrees with symmetry.
common_mistake: Subtracting a hole area but adding its first moment, or mixing component reference axes.

check.question: How should a cut-out be included in a composite centroid calculation?
options: As negative area and negative first moments
As positive area with no first moment
check.explanation: Subtract both the removed area and its contribution to each first moment.

title: Second moments of area and parallel axes
description: Calculate second moments about a stated area axis using standard shapes and the parallel-axis theorem.
practice_prompt: Find the centroid first. Calculate each component contribution about the same final axis, subtracting cut-outs.
common_mistake: Using area moment in m^4 as though it were mass moment in kg m^2.

check.question: Which is the correct parallel-axis relation for an area?
check.explanation: For an area, the shift term is A d^2 and the units are length to the fourth power.

title: Section properties by integration
description: Choose a differential strip and integrate its area, first moment or second moment about the required axis.
outcomes: Distinguish strip centroids from point coordinates
practice_prompt: Calculate Ix with horizontal strips, then check using vertical strips with the strip second moment included.
common_mistake: Using a finite-depth strip centroid y_c in place of every point coordinate y in the definition of Ix.

check.question: For a vertical strip with finite depth in y, is its contribution to Ix always just y_c^2 dA?
options: No; the strip own centroidal second moment may also contribute
check.explanation: For finite-depth strips, the strip own second moment must be retained. S4 explains this distinction in detail.

title: Particle kinematics: position, velocity and acceleration
description: Choose a coordinate direction and connect position, velocity, acceleration and time using graphs or constant-acceleration relations.
practice_prompt: Sketch s(t), v(t) and a(t) for one simple motion. State when constant-acceleration formulas are valid.
common_mistake: Using a constant-acceleration equation when acceleration changes during the interval.

check.question: When is v^2 = v0^2 + 2a(s-s0) valid with one constant a?
options: When acceleration is constant over the interval
check.explanation: That form follows from constant acceleration and cannot be applied indiscriminately to variable acceleration.

title: Variable acceleration and piecewise motion
description: Select an appropriate differential relationship for a(t), a(s) or a(v), and carry conditions between intervals.
practice_prompt: For a = a(s), start from a = v dv/ds. For a piecewise history, carry the ending state into the next interval.
common_mistake: Resetting velocity or position to zero at the start of every time interval.

check.question: Which relationship is particularly useful when acceleration is given as a function of position?
check.explanation: The chain rule gives a = dv/dt = (dv/ds)(ds/dt) = v dv/ds.

title: Particle force and acceleration
description: Connect a particle free-body diagram to acceleration using Newton second law, including friction and connected bodies.
practice_prompt: Draw the FBD and acceleration direction separately. Derive the normal force before computing kinetic friction.
common_mistake: Assuming N = mg on every inclined or externally pulled surface.

check.question: What does a particle free-body diagram contain?
options: Real external forces on the particle
An extra ma force as well as all real forces
check.explanation: The FBD contains real forces. ma belongs on the acceleration side of Newton second law.

title: Normal-tangential and circular kinetics
description: Resolve force balance along the tangent and inward normal, with a_n = v^2/rho and a_t = dv/dt.
outcomes: Separate speed change from direction change
practice_prompt: At a specified point on a track, draw inward normal and tangent axes, then write their force equations separately.
common_mistake: Setting normal acceleration to zero just because the speed is constant.

check.question: At constant nonzero speed on a circle of radius r, which acceleration remains?
check.explanation: Speed is constant, but velocity direction changes, producing inward normal acceleration.

title: Particle work and energy
description: Connect net work over a displacement to a change in particle kinetic energy, including springs and friction.
outcomes: Identify positive, negative and zero work
practice_prompt: Draw initial and final states, list the work of each force, and use T1 + sum U = T2.
common_mistake: Using energy alone to answer a question asking directly for elapsed time.

check.question: A constant kinetic friction force opposes a nonzero displacement. What is its work on the body?
check.explanation: The friction force is opposite displacement, so its dot product with displacement is negative.

title: Potential energy, power and method choice
description: Choose between force-acceleration, work-energy and conservation of mechanical energy; include nonconservative work and power appropriately.
outcomes: Choose a method from the requested unknown
practice_prompt: For a smooth track with a spring, use energy for speed, then force balance if the question also asks for a normal reaction.
common_mistake: Ignoring friction or motor work while claiming mechanical energy is conserved.

check.question: A particle moves on a rough track. Can T1 + V1 = T2 + V2 be used while ignoring friction work?
options: No, the friction work must be accounted for
check.explanation: Nonconservative work changes mechanical energy; include it in the energy balance.

title: Rigid-body velocity and relative motion
description: Describe translation, fixed-axis rotation and general plane motion using velocity compatibility.
outcomes: Use vB = vA + omega cross rBA
practice_prompt: Write known velocity directions first. Use shared-pin velocity compatibility before solving link angular velocities.
common_mistake: Assigning the velocity of one body point to every point on a rotating rigid body.

check.question: In general plane motion, which relative-velocity relation is correct?
options: vB = omega rBA for every reference point
check.explanation: Translation of A and rotation relative to A both contribute.

title: Instantaneous centres and no-slip velocity transfer
description: Use instantaneous centres for velocity and apply compatible tangential velocities in rolling, gears, belts and pulleys.
practice_prompt: Locate an IC from known velocity directions. Calculate a speed, then check with relative velocity.
common_mistake: Assuming a point with zero instantaneous velocity must also have zero acceleration.

check.question: A rolling wheel has a contact point with zero instantaneous velocity. Must that point acceleration also be zero?
options: Only when the wheel radius is known
check.explanation: An instantaneous zero-velocity point need not be a zero-acceleration point.

title: Rigid-body acceleration and linked systems
description: Complete velocity analysis, then include tangential and normal terms in relative acceleration with the correct constraints.
outcomes: Include alpha cross r and -omega^2 r
practice_prompt: Write aB = aA + alpha cross rBA - omega^2 rBA. Label the direction of each term before solving components.
common_mistake: Leaving out the normal omega^2 r term or treating the instantaneous centre as a fixed pin.

check.question: Which acceleration term points from B towards A in the standard relative-acceleration equation?
check.explanation: The normal term -omega^2 rBA points towards the reference point.

title: Mass moment of inertia and rigid-body kinetic energy
description: Distinguish mass moment of inertia from area moment, and choose kinetic energy for translation, rotation or general plane motion.
outcomes: Choose IG or a fixed-axis IO
practice_prompt: Classify a sliding block, a pinned rod and a rolling wheel. Write a suitable kinetic-energy expression for each.
common_mistake: Using an area second moment in a rotational kinetic-energy expression.

check.question: For a rigid body in general plane motion, which expression is valid using its mass centre G?
check.explanation: General plane motion combines mass-centre translation and rotation about G.

title: Rigid-body work-energy and rolling systems
description: Apply work-energy to translating and rotating bodies, including force work, couple work and rolling constraints.
practice_prompt: Draw the two configurations, include both kinetic-energy terms, list work terms and apply a valid rolling constraint.
common_mistake: Omitting rotational energy or automatically counting static rolling friction as energy loss.

check.question: In pure rolling without slip on a stationary surface, what is the speed relation for wheel centre G?
check.explanation: The no-slip velocity constraint gives vG = r omega.
